subject: Security follow-up & subprocessor catalog request — post-demo
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@healthbridge.com>, Markus Vogel <mvogel@healthbridge.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Jul 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + security items we promised (post-demo)

Hi Laura / Markus,

Thanks again for the demo time today — great questions and very helpful context on your data residency needs and HIPAA scope. Per our conversation I wanted to bundle the immediate follow-ups so you have a single reference: 

- SOC 2 status: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II in May 2027; I attached the summary control map. Full report can be shared under NDA.
- GDPR/HIPAA: We support both; our default hosted product keeps customer datasets isolated per-tenant and we offer private deployment options if you require on-prem or VPC-only routing.
- Subprocessors: I've attached a current extract of our subprocessor catalog (redwood_subprocessors_v1.xlsx). Key callouts: AWS (us-west-2) for compute & S3, GCP for embeddings batching (eu-west for EU customers), and Logstash partner for aggregated logs.
- Next steps I promised today: 1) Laura to confirm which of the two flows (hosted vs private) you want to validate first; 2) HealthBridge to send any required template for background checks/artifacts; 3) Redwood to initiate the vendor security questionnaire (we can fill your questionnaire or ours).

Action: Laura — can you confirm whether you want the hosted POC in us-west or we should plan for a VPC trial? If hosted, we'll provide a scoped evidence package within 48 hours.

Best,
Ben

--
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0189

Subject: Re: Quick recap + security items we promised (post-demo)

Thanks Ben — useful recap. A couple clarifying points: 

1) For the POC we prefer hosted in us-west to start; if the throughput looks good we'll evaluate Dedicated.
2) We need confirmation that log exports to third-party analytics are optional / disabled by default; our security team flagged log forwarding.
3) Can you confirm whether any subprocessors have access to plaintext customer data (not just telemetry)?

I'll loop in our security lead if needed. Also attached is our standard vendor security questionnaire — if Redwood can complete Section A and B this week that would help accelerate procurement.

Laura

Ben — forwarding Laura's note. Tagging Soojin (infosec) and Marissa (legal) for two quick asks:

1) Soojin: confirm whether any subprocessor in the attached catalog has access to plaintext customer PII/PHI. From my quick pass: compute (AWS/GCP) access is managed by infra roles; Logstash partner receives only anonymized logs — but need confirmation for HIPAA concerns.

2) Marissa: if we need to sign a CDA/NDA to transfer the SOC2 report, let me know and I can prepare. Laura offered HealthBridge questionnaire; we should decide whether to fill theirs or send our standard questionnaire response.

Priyom
Account Success (covering POC ops)
priom.das@redwood.ai

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priom.das@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Jul 2028 13:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Security follow-up & subprocessor catalog request — action items for security/legal

Priyom / team — quick answers after a quick inventory: 

- Subprocessors with potential access to plaintext data: none by default for hosted POC. Compute (AWS us-west-2) nodes run customer processes in tenant-isolated containers and we encrypt at rest and in transit. The only exception historically was a support diagnostic flow (rare, on approval) where logs could contain redacted snippets; our default support tooling strips PHI/PII.
- Log forwarding: disabled by default. Customers must opt-in for third-party analytics exports; we can provide configuration to blacklist specific fields.
- SOC2 report: available under NDA; control mapping attached (see security_questionnaire_Redwood.docx).

I'll prepare a short statement for procurement: 1) list of subprocessors with roles and access level; 2) confirmation that no subprocessor has routine access to plaintext PHI for hosted POC. I can have that out by EOD tomorrow.

Sooj
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai

- Please go ahead and complete Sections A & B of the attached questionnaire and provide the subprocessor CSV with a column for 'data access level' (none / metadata / plaintext redacted / plaintext).
